choices.title: Recovery Companion
choices.description: A personal AI companion translates Arthur’s changing recovery plan into clear daily next steps through voice, visual, wearable or accessible interfaces.
choices.space:
Existing home remains substantially unchanged.
Comfortable interaction from Arthur’s preferred chair, table or bedside.
Readable viewing angles, normal residential acoustics and lighting, and multimodal controls.
choices.engineering:
Convenient power and charging, reliable residential connectivity, secure identity and replaceable consumer interfaces.
Local processing for selected private interactions where appropriate.
choices.operating: The care team must define the authoritative plan, content governance, clinical limits, escalation triggers and ownership of conflicting instructions.
choices.limit: Accurate guidance may still be physically difficult or impossible to perform in the existing home.
choices.mayShow: Arthur in a recognizable home using discreet voice or visual guidance and a short daily plan.
choices.mustNotShow: Whole-home sensing, adapted rehab space, robotics, automatic diagnosis or clinicians automatically present.

choices.title: Recovery-Supportive Home
choices.description: Arthur’s approved recovery plan becomes part of selected home routines and places, with contextual support appearing where activity occurs.
choices.space:
Purposeful relationships among activity, rest, nutrition and medication routines.
Recovery-supportive zones, accessible storage, comfortable rest locations, adjustable lighting and contextual information touchpoints.
Selective, reversible adaptations rather than a total renovation.
choices.engineering: Reliable connectivity, local device communication, distributed power, maintainable pathways, household controls, manual fallback and privacy-conscious commissioning.
choices.operating: The home must know which plan is current, avoid reinforcing completed or outdated tasks, and maintain ordinary operation during outages.
choices.limit: The home can reinforce a plan but cannot determine whether a symptom is clinically significant or whether the plan should change.
choices.mayShow: A recognizable home with selective adaptations, contextual guidance, adjustable lighting and organized routine-support areas.
choices.mustNotShow: Medical equipment throughout the house, whole-home robotics, autonomous clinical decisions, ubiquitous screens or perfect accessibility.

choices.title: Recovery Coach
choices.description: AI organizes recovery information while a consistent human coach helps Arthur interpret choices, adjust routines and remain engaged.
choices.space:
A flexible, private interaction setting at Arthur’s preferred chair or table.
Good lighting, glare control, acoustic clarity, shared viewing and optional caregiver participation.
choices.engineering: Reliable secure communications, accessible controls, current shared recovery information and alternative communication methods.
choices.operating: Coach availability, continuity, scope, manageable caseload, protected time and escalation access are required.
choices.limit: Human continuity, authority and capacity are finite; the coach cannot remove physical barriers or create clinical resources.
choices.mayShow: Arthur in a comfortable home setting with a consistent coach, shared information and optional caregiver participation.
choices.mustNotShow: Permanent clinician presence, instant 24-hour access, complete home adaptation, ambient monitoring or unlimited coach authority.

choices.title: Guided Movement
choices.description: Wearables, spatial sensing and AI adjust clinically governed movement guidance while Arthur uses the existing home.
choices.space:
Identify usable existing activity zones without implying comprehensive redesign.
Provide lighting, sightlines, sensor positioning and feedback Arthur can receive while moving.
choices.engineering: Local sensing, connectivity, charging/storage, privacy controls, replaceable interfaces and safe fallback when sensing fails.
choices.operating: Clinical rehabilitation governance remains essential; movement observation does not establish medical safety.
choices.limit: The home’s stairs, thresholds, furniture and circulation barriers remain.
choices.mayShow: Arthur moving through the existing home with subtle wearable or spatial guidance.
choices.mustNotShow: Remodeled home, structural supports, robotics, whole-home sensing or automatic clinical clearance.

choices.title: Recovery-Ready Home
choices.description: The home provides more support early and allows selected support to recede or be repurposed as Arthur regains independence.
choices.space:
Comfortable circulation, rest points, adaptable furniture, thoughtful relationships among daily spaces and predictable engineered supports.
Adjustable task lighting, glare control, low-force hardware, adaptable storage, bathroom/activity support and usable controls.
choices.engineering: Structural backing, distributed power/controls, maintainable actuators, manual overrides, replaceable components and fail-safe load paths.
choices.operating: The home cannot interpret concerning fatigue, prescribe rehabilitation progression or establish clinical safety.
choices.limit: Clinical change is not recognized automatically, and adaptation cannot make medically inappropriate activity safe.
choices.mayShow: Selective remodeling, adaptable fixtures, clear movement routes, rest locations and a familiar home.
choices.mustNotShow: Clinical assessment, autonomous exercise prescribing, robotics, comprehensive sensing or fully autonomous home.

choices.title: Robotic Assistance
choices.description: One selected wearable or environmental robotic intervention temporarily extends Arthur’s ability to perform a defined everyday task.
choices.space: Robot-compatible movement paths, floor transitions, thresholds, safe interaction zones and furniture clearances appropriate to the selected device.
choices.engineering: Discreet charging/docking, communications, collision avoidance, maintenance/storage, accessible controls, predictable stopping and manual disengagement.
choices.operating: Reliability, training, maintenance, cost, trust, safe use and clinical appropriateness remain dependencies.
choices.limit: Device dependence, limited operating range, charging, maintenance and technology lifecycle.
choices.mayShow: A believable lightweight assistive device helping with one task, supported by targeted home adaptations.
choices.mustNotShow: Humanoid servants, autonomous living, unlimited assistance, whole-home transformation or clinical judgment.

choices.title: Wearable Signals
choices.description: Wearable and personal devices capture selected recovery indicators and identify changes that deserve attention or review.
choices.space:
Existing home remains unchanged except for convenient device-use, charging, storage and measurement locations.
Accessible notifications for changes in vision, hearing, dexterity and fatigue.
choices.engineering: Reliable connectivity, charging, offline behavior, device integration, data-quality provenance and replaceable wearables.
choices.operating: The system must distinguish missing data from reassuring data and define thresholds, alert ownership and fallback.
choices.limit: Missing, poor or ignored measurements; alert burden; one data stream lacks broader context.
choices.mayShow: Arthur in the existing home with one unobtrusive wearable and restrained recovery information.
choices.mustNotShow: Ambient home sensing, clinical monitoring station, diagnosis, automatic response or multiple devices covering Arthur.

choices.title: Ambient Recovery
choices.description: Selected home areas observe recovery-relevant changes in function and routine with minimal active effort from Arthur.
choices.space:
Deliberate sensing geography for selected transitions and activities, with explicit unsensed privacy zones.
Sensors integrated discreetly into appropriate ceilings, lighting, fixtures or furnishings.
choices.engineering:
Power, networking, local/edge processing, secure controls, maintainable service locations and replaceable technology.
Household consent, data retention/access governance and independent ordinary controls for lighting, doors and heating.
choices.operating: Environmental observations require interpretation; household privacy, consent, maintenance and false context remain critical.
choices.limit: A changed pattern may reflect weather, visitors, pain, fatigue or routine rather than clinical deterioration.
choices.mayShow: Almost invisible sensing at selected locations, Arthur living normally and subtle indication of activity change.
choices.mustNotShow: Cameras everywhere, holographic analytics, clinical monitoring room, diagnosis or automatic emergency intervention.

choices.title: Recovery Forecast
choices.description: AI aggregates legitimate available information and identifies deviation from Arthur’s individualized expected recovery trajectory.
choices.space:
Minimal home alteration; Arthur reviews forecasts privately in an ordinary comfortable location.
Interfaces communicate concern, uncertainty and data gaps accessibly.
choices.engineering:
Baseline inputs: clinical/discharge information, prescribed targets, Arthur-reported symptoms and follow-up data.
Earned: longitudinal aggregation, individualized trajectory modeling, trend interpretation and explanation.
Wearable, ambient and instrumented rehab data require separate selected investments.
choices.operating: Data completeness, provenance, predictive validity, bias, model drift, false alarms and clinical interpretation remain dependencies.
choices.limit: Prediction may be incomplete, inaccurate or overconfident and remains neither diagnosis nor response.
choices.mayShow: Arthur in an almost unchanged home reviewing a restrained forecast with uncertainty and data gaps.
choices.mustNotShow: Omniscient digital twin, holographic Arthur, magical sensors, autonomous diagnosis, automatic response or guaranteed prediction.

choices.title: Right Help, Right Time
choices.description: AI uses available context to identify and initiate an appropriate response pathway without requiring Arthur to navigate the system alone.
choices.space: Accessible interaction from ordinary home locations, multimodal access, lighting, acoustic clarity and privacy suitable for a concern.
choices.engineering: Resilient communications, power, secure contextual exchange, fallback channels and a clearly distinct emergency route.
choices.operating: Closed-loop handoff required: recommendation, request, receipt and accepted responsibility. Routing is not completed care.
choices.limit: Correct routing does not create service availability, timeliness, capacity or interoperability.
choices.mayShow: Arthur connecting through a discreet interface with relevant context accompanying the request.
choices.mustNotShow: Instant clinician access, automatic treatment, complete interoperability, renovation or robotic intervention.

choices.title: Care Comes Home
choices.description: For explicitly eligible episodes, Arthur’s existing home temporarily supports appropriate assessment or selected care and then returns to ordinary use.
choices.space: A defined temporary care zone with clear space, repositionable furniture, stable positions, assessment lighting, acoustic privacy, accessible routes and nearby hygiene.
choices.engineering: Rated power, secure connectivity, portable diagnostics, safe cabling, equipment positioning/removal, environmental suitability, sanitation and transfer fallback.
choices.operating: Clinical eligibility, available mobile workforce, equipment logistics, staff safety, infection prevention, supervision and transfer capability are required.
choices.limit: The home cannot support every intervention and home-care staff/equipment remain finite.
choices.mayShow: A believable home assessment with selected portable equipment, clinician participation and discreet temporary adaptation.
choices.mustNotShow: Permanent clinical room, ICU equipment, autonomous treatment, unlimited home care or guaranteed transfer avoidance.

choices.title: Recovery Navigator
choices.description: One accountable person recognizes the unresolved need, connects Arthur to the next service, confirms receipt and follows through until responsibility is accepted.
choices.space:
At home: private accessible interaction, reliable communication, shared restricted information and caregiver participation.
Across care: physical/virtual handoff points and distributed navigator work settings.
choices.engineering: Role-appropriate mobile information, cross-service communications, supported escalation and continuity mechanisms when the assigned navigator is unavailable.
choices.operating: Manageable workload, defined authority, cross-service relationships, current context, backup coverage and available resources.
choices.limit: The navigator cannot create capacity, clinical authority, transport, eligibility or unavailable services.
choices.mayShow: Arthur communicating with one recognizable navigator while appropriate services connect through discreet channels.
choices.mustNotShow: Omnipotent concierge, instant universal access, command center or autonomous cross-provider coordination.
